etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English monk, from Old English munuc, from Proto-West Germanic *munik, from Late Latin monicus, variant of monachus, from Ancient Greek μοναχός (monakhós, “single, solitary”), from μόνος (mónos, “alone”).

definitions.definition: A male member of a monastic order who has devoted his life for religious service.

quote.citation: 1802, Joseph Ritson, “Poets of the Fifteenth Century”, in Bibliographia Poetica‎[1]:
quote.text: This is believed to be the completeſt liſt of this voluminous, proſaick, and driveling monk, that can be formed, without acceſs, at leaſt, to every manuſcript library in the kingdom, which would be very difficult, if not imposſible, to obtain.

quote.citation: 1982, Michael Bishop, No enemy but time:
quote.text: In clusters on the plain, like cowlless monks at matins, sat the vultures that had settled on the corpse of the hyena impaled by the female rhino  […]

definitions.definition: In earlier usage, an eremite or hermit devoted to solitude, as opposed to a cenobite, who lived communally.

quote.citation: 1907 January, Harold Bindloss, chapter 20, in The Dust of Conflict, 1st Canadian edition, Toronto, Ont.: McLeod & Allen, →OCLC:
quote.text: Tony's face expressed relief, and Nettie sat silent for a moment until the vicar said “It was a generous impulse, but it may have been a momentary one, while in the case of monk and crusader there must have been a sustaining purpose, and possibly a great abnegation, a leaving of lands and possessions.”

definitions.definition: (slang) A male who leads an isolated life; a loner, a hermit.
(slang) An unmarried man who does not have sexual relationships.
A South American monkey (Pithecia monachus); also applied to other species, as Cebus xanthosternos.
The bullfinch, common bullfinch, European bullfinch, or Eurasian bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula).

quote.citation: 1990, Honoré de Balzac, James Lewis May, Jean de Boschère, Ten droll tales, page 25:
quote.text: "Ah!" she cried, "thou art the prettiest little monk that ever monked it in this blessed, amorous town of Constance!"

quote.citation: 2002, David Pownall, Plays two - Volume 2, →ISBN, page 41:
quote.text: Good people, if you're ever short of a job, don't take up monking for a living.

definitions.definition: To act like a monk; especially to be contemplative.

quote.text: Many a scholar, making wings of candlewicks to flap away old darkness, monked his life to fasting long while feasting upon new light.
...drinking: monking on a mountain: plodding in self-inflicted darkness so that the entrance into light would be heightened and supercharged: sacrifice and gain: the meek shall inherit the earth.

quote.citation: 2001, Kevin Everod Quashie, R. Joyce Lausch, Keith D. Miller, New Bones: Contemporary Black Writers in America, page 482:
quote.text: Sometimes, in the joint, time gets long. It's best then to just sit and think. I call it "monking," because you can become so inspired, with revelations and understandings. After a monking spell, you may get angry in a strange way.

quote.citation: 2017, Neil McKenty, In the Stillness Dancing: The Journey of John Main, →ISBN:
quote.text: There were half-serious references to his 'going monking'; his new 'religion'; his grey habit; the magnificent house presented to the community in Montreal, etc. (“What price the vow of poverty, etc.”)

definitions.definition: To monkey or meddle; to behave in a manner that is not systematic.

quote.citation: 2015, Tooty Nolan, Earplug Adventures: An Exaltation of Earplugs, →ISBN:
quote.text: The Avatar spoke gently as she responded to his jibe. "Now fucking get aboard and stop monking on like a schoolboy, you silly earplug.

"You just go into the swamp and keep monking around, and maybe in a week er so, somebody'll open up and begin shooting at you, and if you live long enough to git curious about it, that'll be Tom Keefer."

quote.citation: 2016, Ring Lardner, Treat 'Em Rough - Letters From Jack The Kaiser Killer, →ISBN:
quote.text: ... because when a man is a corporal its all head work you might say and a man ought to keep their mind on their job evenings as well as day times and I felt like I couldn't do that and be monking with French at the same time...

quote.citation: 2011, Devon W. Carbado, Dwight A. McBride, Donald Weise, Black Like Us: A Century of Lesbian, Gay, and Bisexual African American Fiction, →ISBN:
quote.text: I looked up from the thick cotton mat, unsure where my legs were. “She looks monked up.” “maybe her brain is damaged, huh, miss Bryant?”

quote.citation: 2015, Tonya Craft, Accused: My Fight for Truth, Justice, and the Strength to Forgive, →ISBN:
quote.text: She looked down at herself and said, “Oh, I got that from monking.” “From what?” “Monking. You ain't never done meth, girl?” she said.

definitions.definition: To be attached in a way that sticks out.

quote.citation: 1981, Kalu Uka, A Consummation of Fire: A Novel, page 9:
quote.text: Molten roofing north, lead dripping down south, stand like those immobilized columns of arctic water west, stalagmites, monked and housed or stamped and dudleyed east, in school texts.
All these controls and screens are monked on to a massive network of computers that coordinates the sights.
Those shelters formed chapels where aged forms of the implants monked out in built cells, little churchy cells that perished or grew plain, quivering and hidden from sight under alders.

quote.citation: 1932, Delos W. Lovelace, King Kong, published 1965, page 64:
quote.text: ‘We wuz talkin’ and the monk got loose, and she sent me off to catch him.’
